investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be missing and all contract assertions to go unverified. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, and preemption cannot free capacity because no lower-priority victims exist. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state and never reaches a running, idle, or ready state. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a scheduled pod, so it cannot populate vmIdPresent or remoteState, and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) is violated in full.

investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for check `image-generation-stream` failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a `credit_balance_exhausted` error. investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account associated with the API key used by the eval runner at `/api/generate/image/stream` has exhausted its credit balance. The OpenAI API returned HTTP error code `credit_balance_exhausted` with type `insufficient_quota`, which the AURA backend translated into a `generation_error` SSE frame with code `GENERATION_FAILED`. Because the stream never emitted a `generation_completed` frame and never produced an image URL, both assertions in the expected-output contract (`frameTypes contains "generation_completed"` and `imageUrlPresent equals true`) failed. This is an eval infrastructure / API credential issue, not a code defect. No evidence of a user-facing production outage is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.title: Image Generation Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for check `image-generation-stream` failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a `credit_balance_exhausted` error. The SSE stream terminated with a `generation_error` frame instead of the required `generation_completed` frame, and no image URL was produced, violating both assertions in the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account associated with the API key used by the eval runner at `/api/generate/image/stream` has exhausted its credit balance. The OpenAI API returned HTTP error code `credit_balance_exhausted` with type `insufficient_quota`, which the AURA backend translated into a `generation_error` SSE frame with code `GENERATION_FAILED`. Because the stream never emitted a `generation_completed` frame and never produced an image URL, both assertions in the expected-output contract (`frameTypes contains "generation_completed"` and `imageUrlPresent equals true`) failed. This is an eval infrastructure / API credential issue, not a code defect. No evidence of a user-facing production outage is present in the supplied packet.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1242 — the call returned in ~1.2 seconds, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a timeout or network failure.
expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 339-344): assertions require frameTypes contains generation_completed AND imageUrlPresent equals true — both violated.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be missing and all contract assertions to go unverified. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, and preemption cannot free capacity because no lower-priority victims exist. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state and never reaches a running, idle, or ready state. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a scheduled pod, so it cannot populate vmIdPresent or remoteState, and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) is violated in full.

The snapshot was 479 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-08-11T20:41:39.952Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 7 hours and 59 minutes before the eval — roughly 179 minutes beyond the contract's maximum allowed age. This is an eval-layer signal of a missed or failed workflow run; no evidence of a user-facing production outage is present in the supplied packet.
